# EEPROM golden banks

The four `.bin` files are EEPROM pflash images for MINI404, generated by the
firmware repository's own generator. `TestBanksMatchTheVendorGenerator` fails
when our port in `eeprom.go` and the format real firmware reads diverge. They are generated configuration data, not
vendor code.

## Files

| path | content |
|---|---|
| `bank1.bin` | one journal transaction: the wizard-skip items plus the Connect seed with a preset token |
| `bank2.bin` | erased, 8192 bytes of `0xFF`, which is the state the vendor harness leaves the second bank in |
| `no-token-bank1.bin` | the same seed with `Connect Token` omitted, for the registration lane |
| `no-token-bank2.bin` | erased |

## Seed

| field | value |
|---|---|
| host | `10.0.2.2`, the QEMU user-network address of the host |
| port | 8080 |
| tls | false |
| token | `0123456789abcdefghij`, twenty characters, the longest the field holds |
| enabled | true |

The wizard-skip items are `DEFAULT_EEPROM_CONTENT` from the vendor harness at
`tests/integration/conftest.py`: `Run Selftest`, `Run XYZ Calibration`,
`Run First Layer` and `FSensor Enabled` all false, and
`Selftest Result Gears` as 21 bytes of `0xAA`.

## Regenerating after a firmware bump

Regenerate deliberately, never by editing a byte in an editor. A diff here means the
vendor format, an item name or an item's C++ type moved, and the change belongs
in `eeprom.go` with the fixture regenerated in the same commit.

Regenerate with the firmware repository's own generator, never with `eeprom.go`.
A fixture produced by the code under test proves nothing, so the recipe below
drives `utils/persistent_stores/eeprom.py` from a Prusa-Firmware-Buddy checkout
with its own tooling. It needs no firmware build and nothing beyond that
repository's standard library.

Run it from a checkout of the firmware, with `OUT` pointing at this directory:

```sh
OUT=/path/to/prusa-connect/tools/mini404/testdata/eeprom
python3 - "$OUT" <<'GEN'
import struct, sys
sys.path.insert(0, 'utils')
from persistent_stores import eeprom

out = sys.argv[1]
wizard_skip = [
    ('Run Selftest', b'\x00'),
    ('Run XYZ Calibration', b'\x00'),
    ('Run First Layer', b'\x00'),
    ('FSensor Enabled', b'\x00'),
    ('Selftest Result Gears', 21 * b'\xaa'),
]

def fixed(text, size):
    raw = text.encode('utf-8')
    return raw + b'\x00' * (size - len(raw))

def write(prefix, token):
    items = list(wizard_skip) + [('Connect Host', fixed('10.0.2.2', 21))]
    if token:
        items.append(('Connect Token', fixed(token, 21)))
    items += [
        ('Connect Port', struct.pack('<H', 8080)),
        ('Connect TLS', b'\x00'),
        ('Connect Enabled', b'\x01'),
    ]
    image = eeprom.generate_bank(sequence_id=1, version=1, items=items)
    open(f'{out}/{prefix}bank1.bin', 'wb').write(image.ljust(8192, b'\xff'))
    open(f'{out}/{prefix}bank2.bin', 'wb').write(b'\xff' * 8192)

write('', '0123456789abcdefghij')
write('no-token-', '')
GEN
```

The field sizes are `sizeof(std::array<char, connect_host_size + 1>)` and its
token twin from
`src/persistent_stores/store_instances/config_store/constants.hpp`. The journal
terminates the firmware if a record's length is not exactly the `sizeof` of its
item's type, so they are exact. `sequence_id=1` and `version=1` are what the
vendor harness passes.

## Where the sizes come from

| number | source |
|---|---|
| file size 8192 | the size the vendor harness creates both bank files at, and the drive MINI404 mounts with `-drive if=pflash` |
| first bank offset `0x500` | `start_address` in `src/persistent_stores/store_instances/config_store/backend_instance.hpp` |
| bank size 3408 | `BANK_SIZE`, `(8096 - 0x500) / 2`, from the same header |

`generate_bank` returns 8096 bytes, the firmware's own EEPROM extent. The
remaining 96 bytes of each file are the erase value, so the drive is the full
8 KiB the device is.
